title: PLAYER 2 NEAR MISSES PIN PILLAGERS
why: Suppression (v26.62) counts every round that goes past a hostile pillager, and four inside 1.8 s pin him. On the host only player 2's rounds that LANDED counted (netShotTake ran suppHit on every shot word); his near misses ran the count only on the copy in his own window, which the next snapshot overwrote. So the host pinned a man with any four rounds near him and player 2 needed four hits. Proven in the fixture: four player 2 rounds past a hostile pillager left the host's man at count 0, unpinned. Now player 2's window, at the same near-pass test the host's rounds use (once per round per man, a round that stops on a man never reaches the one behind), counts the round for the host, and once a tenth of a second sends one reliable word {t:'sup',q:{body:count}}; the host counts each body the same number of times (at most 16 a word), so the count is the host's own rule. The shot word no longer counts on its own: a gun round is counted once by its sup word, and the shot word also carries frag, melee, finisher, air strike and screen clear damage, none of which pin when the host deals them. An older host ignores the unknown word.
now: Player 2's fire pins pillagers the same way player 1's does: rounds that go close count, not only the ones that hit.
